one_line: Merchant patrons of the Hoysala era, linked with temple donations, nagara bodies and monetized trade in 12th–13th century Karnataka.

appearance.age_look: early 30s for Ketamalla, late 30s for Kesarasetti; both lean but sturdy, active town-merchant build
appearance.face: Both have oval faces and medium brown complexions; Ketamalla with sharper nose and lively eyes, a small healed scar on his left eyebrow, default expression alert and optimistic; Kesarasetti with broader nose, slightly heavier jaw, calm thoughtful gaze and a faint smile line at the cheeks.
appearance.hair: Ketamalla’s black hair is medium-length, neatly oiled and tied back into a small low knot at the nape, with a thin central part; Kesarasetti’s black hair is slightly shorter, combed back and tied into a compact knot, both wearing a simple narrow off-white cotton headband around the forehead.
appearance.costume: Ketamalla wears a knee-length, side-tied dhoti in unbleached off-white cotton with a narrow dark green border, wrapped securely and pleated in front, paired with a fitted, short-sleeved upper cloth in muted leaf-green cotton that reaches to mid-hip, and a long fine off-white angavastra draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the waist; he has simple leather sandals, a slender gold chain, and a pair of small round gold ear studs. Kesarasetti wears a similar dhoti in soft beige cotton with a maroon border, wrapped slightly higher on the waist and falling just below the knee, a short-sleeved upper cloth in deep maroon reaching to mid-hip, and a slightly heavier cream angavastra with a subtle maroon stripe draped over both shoulders and down the back, plus sturdy leather sandals, a thicker gold neck ring, and small gold hoop earrings; both have discreet cloth waist-belts where a pouch could be tied, and no royal or martial ornaments, keeping a sober merchant look consistent with a Hoysala-town setting.
appearance.signature: A small open cloth coin-pouch held in Kesarasetti’s left hand, showing neatly stacked gold gadyana-like discs, while Ketamalla carries a rolled palm-leaf inscription bundle tied with a thin cord in his right hand.

ref_desc: Ketamalla and Kesarasetti are lean brown-complexioned Hoysala merchants with tied-back black hair, simple headbands, off-white dhotis, green and maroon upper cloths, cream angavastras, leather sandals, modest gold jewellery, a cloth coin-pouch and a rolled palm-leaf bundle in off-white, green, maroon and gold tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character pair of Ketamalla and Kesarasetti standing side by side in a 12th–13th century Hoysala town setting, shown clearly from head to toe so their design can be reused consistently. Ketamalla appears in his early thirties, lean with a medium brown complexion, an oval face, sharp nose, lively eyes and a small scar on his left eyebrow, expression alert and optimistic. His black hair is oiled and tied into a small low knot at the nape with a thin central part, and he wears a narrow off-white cotton headband. His costume is an off-white knee-length dhoti with a dark green border, neatly pleated and side-tied, a fitted short-sleeved leaf-green upper cloth to mid-hip, and a long fine off-white angavastra draped from his left shoulder across the chest and around the waist, plus simple leather sandals, a slender gold chain and small round gold ear studs. Kesarasetti is late thirties, lean but slightly broader, medium brown complexion, oval face with broader nose and heavier jaw, calm thoughtful gaze and faint smile lines. His black hair is combed back and tied in a compact knot, also with a narrow off-white headband. He wears a beige dhoti with a maroon border, wrapped to fall just below the knee, a deep maroon short-sleeved upper cloth to mid-hip, and a cream angavastra with a subtle maroon stripe draped over both shoulders and down the back, sturdy leather sandals, a thicker gold neck ring and small gold hoop earrings, with simple cloth waist-belts on both men. In Kesarasetti’s left hand show a small open cloth coin-pouch revealing neat stacks of gold discs; in Ketamalla’s right hand show a tightly rolled palm-leaf inscription bundle tied with a cord. Use off-white, leaf-green, maroon, beige and gold as the dominant colours, and emphasize dignified merchant patrons in realistic Hoysala-era town dress, drawn in clear anime style without any text or labels.
